nodes.name: Helium pressurant supply
nodes.description: Merchant liquid/gaseous helium used to pressurize ground and flight fluid systems, purge propellant lines, and provide cryogenic cool-down for reusable-launch operations. It is the most supply-concentrated propellant-lane input: helium is a by-product of a handful of natural-gas fields and a small set of producers, and it is periodically short, so launch operators must secure dedicated supply (e.g. the NASA-Air Products sole-source liquid-helium contract for KSC/Cape Canaveral).

metrics.name: US helium use in aerospace, pressurizing and purging
metrics.description: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (helium): of estimated US Grade-A and gaseous helium apparent consumption in 2023, 'aerospace, pressuring, and purging' accounted for 9%. Demand-side end-use share, not a launch-specific figure.

metrics.name: US helium import sources (2019-22)
metrics.description: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (helium): US import sources 2019-2022. Illustrates how geographically concentrated merchant helium supply is.

nodes.notes: Single/near-single-source corner of the propellants lane: helium is a periodically-short, by-product commodity concentrated in a few fields (US + Qatar dominant) and a handful of producers. The 2022 episode (NASA's $1.07B sole-source liquid-helium award to Air Products for KSC launch operations) is the canonical chokepoint. Reusable-launch operators draw on the same concentrated merchant network.

nodes.name: Liquid oxygen (LOX) supply
nodes.description: Merchant liquid oxygen used as the oxidizer for both kerolox (Falcon 9 / Merlin) and methalox (Starship / Raptor) reusable-launch propellant systems. LOX is produced by cryogenic air separation; the merchant supply is an oligopoly of industrial-gas majors. For high-cadence reusable launch the binding constraint is dedicated air-separation capacity and cryogenic-tanker delivery sited near the launch site, which is why Linde is building/operating dedicated air-separation units at Brownsville (Starbase) and Mims, Florida (Cape-area launches).
nodes.notes: Genuinely merchant tier. Named supplier where a specific contract exists: Linde (dedicated Brownsville ASU for SpaceX Starbase; Mims, FL plant for a 'major space launch company' in Florida). Air Liquide is a supplemental/historical KSC supplier. The 2021 COVID LOX shortage (dev set rl_dev_lox_covid_shortage_2021) hit the shared merchant LOX supply/delivery network rather than one named producer.

nodes.name: Liquid methane (LCH4) supply
nodes.description: Rocket-grade liquid methane (LCH4) used as the fuel for the methalox Starship/Super Heavy reusable system. Unlike LOX and helium, methane is not an air-separation product: SpaceX buys liquefied natural gas (LNG, predominantly methane) and purifies/conditions it to rocket-grade, drawing on the natural-gas / LNG merchant network (LNG terminals near Brownsville) rather than the industrial-gas majors. This is a distinct supply chain (cryogenic natural-gas liquefaction and trucking) and is comparatively less concentrated, though rocket-grade purity and cryogenic-tanker logistics still gate cadence.
nodes.notes: Distinct merchant network from LOX/helium: LNG/natural-gas, not air separation. No single industrial-gas major is the named methane producer; SpaceX sources purified LNG from the natural-gas supply chain (Brownsville LNG terminals nearby) and has at times signaled intent to produce its own. Grey-tier pointers (blogs) name a logistics carrier 'GenOx' for liquid-methane trucking to Boca Chica and Air Liquide for LOX, but these are not quality sources for a supplier claim and are intentionally not modeled as named-supplier edges here. Left as a decomposition frontier for the upstream pass (round 2) to resolve the rocket-grade LNG producers/conditioners.

nodes.name: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.
nodes.description: US-headquartered (Allentown, PA) industrial-gas major; one of the big-five global industrial-gas producers and a leading helium supplier to the space-launch industry. Awarded NASA's sole-source liquid-helium supply contract (33 million liters, ~$1.07B) for Kennedy Space Center / Cape Canaveral launch operations, including its proprietary liquid-helium pumps.
nodes.notes: Investor relevance: most direct public exposure to launch-grade helium supply (the propellant lane's tightest corner). Helium is a small slice of APD revenue, so exposure is thematic not material; ticker APD verified on NYSE this round.

nodes.name: Nippon Sanso Holdings Corporation (Matheson)
nodes.description: Japan-headquartered industrial-gas major (formerly Taiyo Nippon Sanso); fourth/fifth-largest global industrial-gas group, majority-owned by Mitsubishi Chemical Group. Its US operating company is Matheson Tri-Gas (Irving, TX). Describes itself as one of only a handful of global helium producers and suppliers, with owned helium-source rights and long-term supply contracts.
nodes.notes: Reported-capable helium/industrial-gas supplier to the launch merchant network (not a confirmed SpaceX-specific contract). One of the 'handful' of global helium producers, so relevant to the concentrated-helium-corner story. Ticker 4091.T verified on Tokyo Stock Exchange this round (parent Mitsubishi Chemical Group holds majority).

nodes.name: Messer SE & Co. KGaA
nodes.description: German family-owned industrial-gas group; describes itself as the largest privately held industrial-gas company in the world and a leading industrial/medical gas company across the Americas, Asia and Europe. In June 2024 it completed the acquisition of the US Federal Helium System (Cliffside Field, reserve, and 423-mile crude-helium pipeline) from the BLM, strengthening its domestic helium position. Long-term minority shareholder is GIC.
nodes.notes: Private (no ticker) per ADR-0009 honesty rule — do NOT assign one. Strategically important to the helium corner because it now owns/operates the Cliffside Federal Helium System, a major US crude-helium source. Models the concentrated-helium-supply structure even though investors cannot hold it directly; minority partner GIC.

edges.claim: Methalox ground propellant operations require merchant helium for pressurizing ground/flight fluid systems and purging propellant lines.
Cryogenic ground loading uses helium as a pressurizing and cool-down/purge agent during propellant conditioning and hold logic.
Subcooled methane/oxygen propellant operations rely on helium for flight/ground pressurization and purge.
The methane/oxygen ground propellant system requires merchant liquid oxygen as oxidizer feedstock for tank-farm loading.
Cryogenic ground loading conditions and loads liquid oxygen as the launch oxidizer.
The methane/oxygen ground propellant system requires rocket-grade liquid methane as the methalox fuel.
Subcooled methane/oxygen propellant operations densify and feed liquid methane fuel.

Air Products holds NASA's sole-source liquid-helium supply contract (33M liters, ~$1.07B) for Kennedy Space Center / Cape Canaveral launch operations, and is a leading helium supplier to the space-launch industry. NASA-named contract, not a SpaceX-specific contract.

Nippon Sanso/Matheson is one of only a handful of global helium producers/suppliers with owned source rights and long-term supply contracts; modeled as capable merchant helium supply, not a confirmed launch-operator contract.

Messer owns and operates the US Federal Helium System (Cliffside crude-helium source and pipeline) acquired from the BLM in June 2024, a major domestic crude-helium source feeding the merchant helium network. Strategic upstream helium position, not a confirmed launch-operator contract.
Air Liquide supplies helium that is indispensable for pressurization, cool-down and cleaning of launch vehicles; modeled as capable merchant helium supply within the industrial-gas oligopoly.

Linde is SpaceX's main industrial-gas supplier of liquid oxygen and nitrogen, building/owning/operating a dedicated air-separation unit at Brownsville, Texas for SpaceX Starbase and supplying a 'major space launch company' in Florida from its Mims air-separation plant.

Air Liquide supplies liquid oxygen (and nitrogen/helium) for launch vehicles and has a long history supporting Kennedy Space Center launches; modeled as a supplemental/capable LOX supplier alongside Linde.
Air Products is a big-five industrial-gas producer of liquid oxygen via air separation; modeled as a capable merchant LOX supplier, not a confirmed launch-operator LOX contract.

evidence.title: NASA Awards Contract for Liquid Helium Acquisition at Kennedy
evidence.summary: NASA selected Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. to supply 33 million liters of liquid helium to Kennedy Space Center under a sole-source contract worth approximately $1.07 billion, including the lease of six proprietary liquid-helium pumps. Helium is used for purging, pressurizing ground/flight fluid systems, and cryogenic cooling in launch operations.
evidence.excerpt: NASA has selected Air Products and Chemicals, Inc of Allentown, Pennsylvania, to supply 33 million liters of liquid helium to the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The sole source contract includes the lease of six proprietary liquid helium pumps. The total value of the contract for the base plus option periods is approximately $1.07 billion. Helium is an inert gas for purging hydrogen systems, a pressurizing agent for ground and flight fluid systems, and a cryogenic cooling agent.
evidence.limitations: NASA agency press release (fetched via WebFetch, 200). Quote condenses four individually-verbatim sentences. This is a NASA (SLS/agency-wide) sole-source helium contract, not a SpaceX-specific contract; used as evidence for the concentrated launch-helium supply structure and Air Products' role, per the 2022 helium dev-set episode.

evidence.title: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Helium
evidence.summary: USGS helium commodity summary: in 2023 US Grade-A and gaseous helium consumption split by end use included 'aerospace, pressuring, and purging' at 9%; US helium imports 2019-22 came mainly from Qatar (47%) and Canada (31%); only a small number of US plants extract and purify helium. Documents the concentrated, by-product nature of helium supply.
evidence.excerpt: aerospace, pressuring, and purging (9%) ... Import Sources (2019-22): Qatar, 47%; Canada, 31%; Algeria, 11%; Russia, 4%; and other, 7%.
evidence.limitations: USGS MCS 2024 helium fact sheet (government primary). PDF rendered binary in WebFetch; text extracted locally from the saved PDF (FlateDecode streams), so excerpt is reconstructed from the decompressed text and should be re-confirmed against the published PDF by the verifier. End-use percentages are US apparent-consumption shares (demand side), not launch-specific or supplier-share figures.

evidence.title: Linde Breaks Ground on $100M Air Separation Plant to Power SpaceX in Brownsville, TX
evidence.summary: Linde broke ground on a $100 million air-separation plant in Brownsville, Texas to supply liquid oxygen and nitrogen directly to SpaceX's Starbase facility for rocket launches, located less than 50 miles from Starbase.
evidence.excerpt: Linde announced it broke ground on a $100 million air separation plant. The modern facility will supply liquid oxygen and nitrogen, essential for rocket launches directly to SpaceX's Starbase facility.
evidence.limitations: Trade-press (ConstructConnect) report, fetched 200. Names SpaceX/Starbase as the customer for the Brownsville LOX/LN2 plant; the Linde corporate release (ev_space_linde_mims_2022 and the 2025 commercial-space release) confirms the ASU and long-term gas agreements but refers only to 'its customer's space operations' without naming SpaceX. Excerpt is two individually-verbatim sentences.

evidence.title: City of Brownsville: Linde to build $100M air separation plant to support SpaceX operations
evidence.summary: City of Brownsville announcement that Linde's new air-separation facility will produce liquid oxygen and nitrogen used in SpaceX's Starship development and launch operations at Starbase, with proximity to SpaceX reducing delivery times for the launch cadence.
evidence.excerpt: The new facility will produce liquid oxygen and nitrogen—two essential gases used in SpaceX's Starship development and launch operations at Starbase. The plant's proximity to SpaceX is expected to significantly reduce delivery times and logistics costs, creating a more efficient supply chain for the private space company's rapid launch cadence.
evidence.limitations: Municipal government announcement (fetched 200), corroborates the SpaceX/Starbase customer identity for the Linde Brownsville LOX/LN2 plant. Local-government press item, not a Linde or SpaceX primary filing; two individually-verbatim sentences.

evidence.title: Linde Signs New Supply Agreement with Major Space Launch Company
evidence.summary: Linde corporate release: signed a long-term agreement with a major space launch company in Florida to supply liquid oxygen and nitrogen from its Mims, Florida air-separation plant, with an expansion at Mims to serve the customer.
evidence.excerpt: Linde today announced it has signed another long-term agreement with a major space launch company in Florida ... Linde will supply the customer with liquid oxygen and nitrogen from its air separation plant at Mims, Florida.
evidence.limitations: Linde IR press release (fetched 200). Confirms a long-term LOX/N2 launch supply agreement and the Mims, FL plant, but the customer is named only as 'a major space launch company' / 'the customer' — SpaceX is NOT named in this Linde primary source (SpaceX naming comes from the secondary Brownsville/ConstructConnect items). Excerpt is two individually-verbatim sentences.

evidence.title: Air Liquide USA — Space market page
evidence.summary: Air Liquide describes supplying liquid hydrogen and oxygen for launch-vehicle propulsion, liquid nitrogen for inerting, and helium for pressurization, cool-down and cleaning, plus decades of cryogenic launch-pad support (Ariane/Kourou). Used as evidence for the role of LOX/LN2/helium in launch operations and Air Liquide's capability as a merchant launch-gas supplier.
evidence.excerpt: supply liquid hydrogen and oxygen for the launch vehicles' propulsion, liquid nitrogen for inerting, and the helium that is indispensable for pressurization, cool-down, and cleaning.
evidence.limitations: Air Liquide vendor/marketing page (sourceStatus vendor_marketing per ADR-0009: fine for who-supplies-what role, weak for share/structure). Verbatim sentence supports the launch-gas roles (LOX/LN2/helium) and Air Liquide capability; the page describes Ariane/Kourou heritage, not a SpaceX-specific contract. Supports the methane node only for the general 'launch propulsion fuels' framing, not a methane supplier claim.

evidence.title: Nippon Sanso Matheson — Helium (He)
evidence.summary: Nippon Sanso/Matheson states it is one of only a handful of global helium producers and suppliers, with owned helium-source rights, a transfill network, and long-term supply contracts with helium producers. Used as evidence for the concentrated helium-supply structure and Nippon Sanso's role.
evidence.excerpt: Nippon Sanso Matheson is one of only a handful of global producers and suppliers of helium. ... Nippon Sanso Matheson's helium position is extremely strong and includes long term supply contracts with helium producers.
evidence.limitations: Vendor/marketing page (vendor_marketing per ADR-0009). The 'one of only a handful of global producers' claim is a vendor self-description corroborated by USGS/market structure (helium is a concentrated, few-source commodity); page lists welding/medical/MRI/leak-detection uses, not space-launch specifically. Two individually-verbatim sentences.

evidence.title: Messer Completes Acquisition of Federal Helium System from BLM
evidence.summary: Messer, the largest privately held industrial-gas company in the world, completed its purchase of the US Federal Helium System (Federal Helium Reserve, Cliffside Field, and 423-mile crude-helium pipeline) from the BLM; Messer had operated the Cliffside Gas Plant under BLM contract since April 2022. Used as evidence for the concentrated domestic helium-supply structure and Messer's upstream helium position.
evidence.excerpt: Messer, the largest privately held industrial gas company in the world ... The Federal Helium System includes the Federal Helium Reserve, the Cliffside Field with its wells and gathering system, the 423-mile-long crude helium pipeline, and additional operational assets. Since April 2022, Messer has operated the Cliffside Gas Plant under contract with the BLM.
evidence.limitations: Messer corporate press release (fetched 200). Confirms Messer's private status, the Federal Helium System assets acquired, and Cliffside operation; does NOT state a global/US helium market-share percentage (the ~15-17% figure seen in secondary market reports is not used here). Excerpt is three individually-verbatim sentences.
